what_it_does.text: Booking.com, part of Booking Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ: BKNG), is an online travel platform connecting travellers with accommodation, flights and car rentals. Since June 2023 it has added generative AI across the booking journey: the AI Trip Planner (built on its own recommendation models and partly on OpenAI's ChatGPT API), Smart Filter and Property Q&A, and from October 2025 its first in-house agentic tools, Smart Messenger and Auto-Reply for partners, alongside AI Trip Support, AI Voice Support and an AI Car Rental Helper for travellers. It also runs an app inside ChatGPT for browsing stays and rental cars, which hands the traveller back to Booking.com to book.

agents.name: AI Trip Planner
agents.what: A conversational planner in the Booking.com app that answers general and property-specific travel questions, suggests destinations and stays, builds itineraries and links straight into the accommodation booking flow. Booking.com says it is evolving into an embedded AI companion across the booking journey.
actions: Recommends destinations and accommodation using Booking.com's existing machine learning models, partly powered by OpenAI's ChatGPT API
Shows a visual list of destinations and properties with Booking.com pricing and deep links
Is integrated into the in-app accommodation booking experience: a tap on a property lets the traveller complete the reservation
Property Q&A: retrieves information from the property listing, traveller reviews and photos to answer specific questions
With a signed-in account, can draw on past searches and travel history (per CNET)
Runs on Booking.com's data platform (BDX), per a vendor case study

agents.name: Smart Messenger
agents.what: A partner-facing agent in the Extranet that helps accommodation partners communicate with guests; paired with Auto-Reply, which answers guest questions instantly from reply topics the partner defines. Booking.com calls these its first customer-facing agentic AI.
actions: Gathers partner, property and reservation information to autonomously take action, knowing when and what to suggest
Generates responses in the partner-to-guest messaging channel
Auto-Reply: instant responses to common and unique guest questions on partner-defined topics
Learns from past interactions and user feedback
Help Me Reply (partner hub): drafts responses to guest messages on the extranet

agents.name: AI Trip Support
agents.what: A 24/7 first point of contact for travellers on customer service topics, helping them find property information and make reservation changes on their own, with handover to a human representative for complex questions.
actions: Gathers relevant information from the property to answer questions such as parking
Supports travellers making reservation changes independently
Hands complex questions over to an informed customer service representative
Live in ten markets including the US, UK, France and Germany

agents.name: AI Voice Support
agents.what: Voice-powered trip management on Booking.com phone lines: callers ask in their own words (for example to cancel a reservation) and the tool pulls their booking details to help, connecting to a human agent when needed.
actions: Pulls the caller's booking details
Handles trip-management requests such as cancellation
Connects to a human agent and passes on all necessary information
Runs on English- and German-speaking phone lines, with Italian and Spanish in testing

agents.name: AI Car Rental Helper
agents.what: Answers common questions about a car rental booking (payment methods, pick-up checklists, insurance) 24/7; Booking.com reports early testing led to fewer support calls, reservation changes and disrupted pickups.
actions: Reads the customer's rental booking and its terms to answer questions
Explains payment methods, pick-up checklists and insurance information
Available in English, French, Spanish, German, Dutch and Italian

use_cases.name: Smart Messenger answers a property's guests
use_cases.who: An accommodation partner in the US, UK, New Zealand or Australia using the Extranet inbox, with Smart Messenger and Auto-Reply switched on (an illustrative case built on the documented features).

reach.what: Partner, property and reservation information, which Smart Messenger gathers to decide what to suggest or do
Guests: suggested replies and instant Auto-Reply answers go to travellers in the partner-to-guest messaging channel
The partner's Extranet inbox, where Smart Messenger, Auto-Reply and Help Me Reply are live
Past interactions and user feedback, from which the agent keeps learning and adapting its responses
Payment requests in the same channel: compromised partner accounts have used Booking.com's official guest messaging to ask guests for card details, with real booking information

mandate.what: Illustrative: suggest replies about the property and the stay; the partner approves each one before it is sent
Illustrative: answer instantly only on the topics the partner has defined in Auto-Reply
Illustrative: never ask a guest for payment or card details in a message

gap.what: Booking.com says Smart Messenger gathers information to autonomously take action; public material does not say which actions it takes without the partner's approval.
The agent writes in the channel that phishing has used to request card details from guests; no public description says how agent messages about payment are limited or marked.
Learning from past interactions: what is kept, and whether it is scoped to one property, is not publicly documented.

controls.what: Auto-Reply answers from custom reply topics the partner defines
Account security: monitoring and blocking of suspicious activity around the clock, and locking or blocking of inactive partner extranet accounts (Booking.com statement, December 2023)

simulation.action: A guest messages the property asking whether early check-in is possible (illustrative)
Smart Messenger gathers the reservation and property details and suggests a reply
The partner approves the suggestion in the Extranet inbox and it is sent
Auto-Reply instantly answers a parking question from a partner-defined topic
A guest asks how to pay the balance; the agent acts on its own and replies with payment instructions taken from an earlier conversation (illustrative)
simulation.note: RiskMandate's record shows an agent message about payment sent in the guest channel without the partner's approval, outside m1 and m3, and lists it as a gap next to the channel's documented phishing history.

simulation.action: Reuses wording learned from a past conversation that included another guest's booking details (illustrative)
simulation.note: RiskMandate's record shows the agent drawing on stored past interactions beyond the current reservation, and records that the scope of that learning is not publicly documented.

simulation.action: The partner reviews the conversation history in the inbox the next morning

use_cases.name: A traveller cancels a stay by phone with AI Voice Support
use_cases.who: A traveller with an existing reservation calling an English- or German-speaking Booking.com support line (an illustrative case built on the documented feature).

reach.what: The caller's booking details, which the tool pulls once connected
Trip management, including cancellation requests; Booking Holdings' CEO says Booking.com customers can now cancel bookings through agentic AI
Property information used to answer questions and support reservation changes (AI Trip Support)
Human customer service agents, who receive the case with all necessary information on handover

mandate.what: Illustrative: act only on the caller's own reservation, after the caller is matched to it
Illustrative: cancel only after reading back the cancellation terms and getting a clear yes
Illustrative: hand to a human for anything outside the property's policy

gap.what: Public material does not say how a caller is matched to a booking before the tool pulls booking details.
Whether the tool completes a cancellation itself or hands it to a person, and what confirmation it asks for, is not publicly documented.

controls.what: Handover to a human agent, who is given all necessary information
A small intent and topic detection model decides whether an issue is self-service or needs a human; unresolved issues go to a human agent
Memory features are offered only with customer consent

simulation.action: The traveller calls and says: I need to cancel my reservation
AI Voice Support pulls the booking details for the caller
Cancels the reservation without reading back the non-refundable charge (illustrative)
simulation.note: RiskMandate's record shows a cancellation completed without the confirmation step in m5, with the booking and the charge it carried.

simulation.action: The caller mentions a second stay booked by a relative; the tool pulls that booking too (illustrative)
simulation.note: RiskMandate's record shows the tool reading a reservation that is not the caller's, outside m4, and lists caller matching as an undocumented gap.

simulation.action: Hands the call to a human agent with the case context

use_cases.name: Planning a trip and booking from the AI Trip Planner
use_cases.who: A signed-in traveller in the Booking.com app planning a family holiday (an illustrative case built on the documented flow).

reach.what: Booking.com's recommendation models and accommodation inventory
Booking.com pricing shown with deep links to property details
The traveller's past searches and travel history when signed in
The in-app accommodation booking flow: one tap on a property to complete the reservation
OpenAI's ChatGPT API, which partly powers the conversation

mandate.what: Illustrative: recommend and show options; a booking happens only when the traveller taps through and confirms
Illustrative: use account history only to personalise this traveller's results

gap.what: Which parts of the conversation and account history reach the third-party model is not publicly documented.
Booking.com's chief business officer named wrong prices and irrelevant content as the failure mode; prices shown in chat are a path to a booking.

controls.what: The reservation is completed by the traveller in the app's booking flow, not in the chat
Launched as a beta for signed-in US Genius members with English settings

simulation.action: Asks for a family-friendly beach stay with a pool for four
Personalises suggestions using the account's past searches and travel history
Sends the conversation, including details from past trips, to the model provider (illustrative)
simulation.note: RiskMandate's record shows account history leaving Booking.com for a third-party model, beyond m8, and marks what is sent as undocumented.

simulation.action: Shows a visual list of properties with prices and deep links
Quotes a price in chat that differs from the live rate on the property page (illustrative)
simulation.note: RiskMandate's record shows the quoted price against the rate the booking flow used, the failure mode Booking.com itself named.

simulation.action: Taps a property and completes the reservation in the app

incidents.what: Phishing through Booking.com's guest messaging: attackers took over hotels' Booking.com accounts, extracted guest booking data and messaged guests demanding card details to avoid cancellation. Booking.com said its backend was not breached and described new measures to lock or block inactive partner extranet accounts. The same channel is where Smart Messenger and Auto-Reply now operate; the incidents did not involve the AI agents.

Reports continue of compromised hotel extranet accounts used to send fraudulent payment requests through the official guest messaging system (not involving its AI agents: the same messaging channel the Smart Messenger agent now uses)

questions: Smart Messenger gathers information to autonomously take action: which actions can it take without the partner approving them, and can a partner require approval for every message?
Guest messaging has been used to phish guests for card details: can Smart Messenger or Auto-Reply ever send or suggest a payment request, and is such a message marked or held?
How is a caller matched to a reservation before AI Voice Support pulls booking details, and does it complete a cancellation itself or hand it to a person?
Which traveller data (conversation, account history, reservation details) is sent to third-party model providers, and is each agent action recorded against the booking it touched?
Press reports an internal agent platform with guardrails for prompt injection and personal data: will Booking.com publish what those guardrails cover for the agents that touch reservations?
